986:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to cut, excavate or trench any right-of-way, road, street, lane, sidewalk, curb or ditch, or other property belonging to the County (for purposes of this section, hereinafter referred to as "County property"), or cause the same to be cut, excavated or trenched without first obtaining a permit from the County.
(b) All digging or excavating to be done, as provided in this section, shall be promptly started and completed without delay after the permit shall have been granted, and such County property shall be, immediately upon the completion of such work, restored to the same or as good a condition as the same was before such work was done thereon. Such work or restoration shall be at all times and in all respects in compliance with the orders and supervision of the County from time to time given to such person for such purpose.
(c) Before any County property is cut, excavated or trenched, an application for a permit must be made to the County. The application must be in writing and set forth the character and location of such work to be done, the probable number of square yards of surface to be removed and the probable date of beginning and the completion of the work. Each application shall be considered by the County road superintendent, who shall, without unreasonable delay, either grant or reject such application. Upon rejection of the application, the applicant shall have the right to present the matter to the Board of Commissioners.
(d) Upon the failure of any person to restore such County property to the same or as good a condition as the same was in before such work was done, in addition to criminal actions provided for in this section, the County is empowered and authorized to cause such repairs to be made so that such County property will be restored to its original condition and the costs thereof, plus 10 percent thereof, shall be charged to and paid by such person who so failed to make such repairs, and such sum shall constitute and be a debt due from such person to the County.
(e) It shall be unlawful for any person to construct a private road or driveway which intersects County property or cause the same to be constructed without first obtaining a permit from the County. That portion of a private road or driveway which is constructed within the County right-of-way must be constructed to the specifications and requirements of the County.
(f) It shall be unlawful for any person to construct a driveway which intersects County property or cause the same to be constructed in such a manner so that dirt, rocks, gravel or other materials wash onto the County property.
(g) It shall be unlawful for any person to fail to comply with any reasonable specifications, requirements, rules or regulations of the County given to such person by the County for the completion of any construction or repairs contemplated by this section.
(h) It shall be unlawful for any person to place or cause to be placed in any County right-of-way, which shall include the ditch and roadway, any dirt, trash, pipe or other material so as to interfere with the drainage or use of said roadway without first obtaining a permit to do so from the County.
(i) It shall be unlawful for any person to damage or destroy any County property. It shall be unlawful for any person to cause damage to any County property.
(j) In addition to subsection (k) of this section for a violation of subsections (e) through (i) of this section, the person so charged shall, upon conviction, be assessed with the costs, plus 10 percent thereof, of repairing or restoring any damaged County property to its original condition.
(k) Any person violating the terms of this section or rules and regulations promulgated pursuant thereto, may be punished per section 1-13. Separate offenses shall be deemed to be committed on each day during or on which a violation occurs or continues.
(Code 2005, § 46-37; Ord. of 1-15-1991, §§ 1—11)

(a) The Board of Commissioners has determined that it would be in the best interest of the citizens of the County to upgrade firefighting services and emergency management services, including rescue and first responder medical assistance (hereinafter collectively referred to as "services") in the unincorporated areas of the County and such areas located within the municipal limits of cities which contract with the County for such services.
(b) The Board of Commissioners has determined that the cost of upgrading County-wide services through the use of ad valorem taxes will create an undue financial burden on the average homeowner.
(c) To provide the services, the Board of Commissioners has determined that it is in the best interest of the citizens of the County to establish a revised special assessment to be levied on structures located in the County Fire and Rescue District.
(d) The annual cost of providing services in the District shall be assessed against the owner of each structure located in the District pursuant to a fee schedule established yearly as a part of the Board of Commissioner's budget.
(e) All structures located within the District shall be liable for assessment, except public buildings and places of religious worship.
(f) Special assessments shall be charged against the owner of a structure if the owner is known and against the structure and the property on which said structure is located if the owner is not known. Life tenants and those who own and enjoy a structure located within the District shall be chargeable with the special assessment thereon. The owner of a structure located within the District on January 1 of each year is liable for the entire special assessment, even if the structure is subsequently sold.

1201:
The rules and regulations governing the administration of claims for tax refunds under this article shall be as follows:
(1) All such claims must be filed with the office of the Board of Commissioners of the County.
(2) Upon receipt of such written claims, the same shall be stamped, showing the date received, which date shall be considered for all purposes the filing date of such tax refund claim.
(3) The claim shall then be referred immediately to the County Attorney and to the Chief Appraiser of the Property Records Department of the County for their review and recommendations.
(4) The findings of the County Attorney and the Chief Appraiser and their recommendations will be passed on to the Board of Commissioners or to the official who has been duly authorized by the Board of Commissioners to approve or disapprove such claims, said recommendations to be made within 30 days from the date said claim is filed in the Board of Commissioner's office.
(5) If the taxpayer or claimant has requested a conference or hearing before the Board of Commissioners in connection with any such refund claim, a date shall be set by the Board of Commissioners or their duly authorized representative within 45 days from the date the claim is filed, and due notice of such hearing shall be given to the taxpayer by regular United States mail to the address given by the taxpayer in the claim form, and such notice is to be mailed at least 3 days prior to such hearing.
(6) If such a hearing is requested and the same is held, the Board of Commissioners or their duly authorized official shall make a determination on such claim within 7 days after such hearing, and the taxpayer shall be informed of the approval or disapproval of the claim by notice in writing addressed to the taxpayer at the address so shown in said claim form and shall be mailed by regular United States mail within 10 days after such hearing.
(7) If the taxpayer does not request a conference or hearing, the Board of Commissioners or their duly authorized official shall notify the taxpayer in writing of his approval or disapproval of the claim within 45 days from the date that the claim is filed, and such notice shall be in writing and is to be mailed to the taxpayer at the address shown in said form, and the same is to be mailed by regular United States mail.
(Code 1983, § 15-17; Code 2005, § 54-33)

1207:
The Board of Commissioners makes the following findings with respect to this article:
(1) State law requires that residents register and license their motor vehicles, tractors, motorcycles and trailers (collectively referred to in this article by the term "motor vehicles") within 30 days after becoming residents of this State. Further, each resident is required to register and license their motor vehicles within 30 days after the purchase, rental or lease of the motor vehicles.
(2) The Board of Commissioners finds that many bona fide residents of the County have moved here from other states and at the time they became residents of the County, their motor vehicles are registered and licensed in the State from which they have moved.
(3) Motor vehicles are subject to ad valorem taxes in this State, which said taxes help to directly fund the schools and County government.
(4) The Board of Commissioners finds that numerous residents of the County have failed to register their motor vehicles in the State within 30 days after becoming residents of the County.
(5) The Board of Commissioners finds that other residents of the County have registered their new or used motor vehicles in other states to avoid paying ad valorem tax.
(6) The Board of Commissioners finds that the failure of these individuals to register their motor vehicles and pay the ad valorem tax on these motor vehicles puts an undue tax burden on the other taxpaying citizens of the County.
(7) The Board of Commissioners finds that, under O.C.G.A. § 40-2-8(a), any person operating a motor vehicle described in O.C.G.A. § 40-2-20 upon any public highway or street without complying with O.C.G.A. § 40-2-20 shall be guilty of a misdemeanor under State law, and that this provision applies to a person who becomes a resident of this State and fails to register his motor vehicle within 30 days after becoming a resident of this State.
(8) The Board of Commissioners finds that the provisions of general law are being evaded because operation of an unregistered motor vehicle without proper registration is a moving offense and, therefore, the motor vehicle must be operated on the public streets or roads in order to be cited for a violation. Because of the County's proximity to Alabama and Tennessee, this makes enforcement of moving violations difficult. The Board of Commissioners desires to provide for local enforcement of this article, which makes it a violation of this Code to fail to register a motor vehicle in the County within 30 days after becoming a resident of this State or for residents to fail to register and license their motor vehicles within 30 days after purchase, rent or lease of the motor vehicle.
(9) The Board of Commissioners finds that the Sheriff, County Police, or County Code Enforcement Officers should enforce this article by issuing a County citation to every resident who fails to register his motor vehicle within 30 days after becoming a resident of this State or within 30 days after acquiring the motor vehicle.
(Code 2005, § 54-71)

1216:
(a) No person shall stop, park or leave standing any unattended motor vehicle upon the paved portion of any County road when it is practicable to stop, park or leave such motor vehicle off the paved portion of such roadway, but in every event an unobstructed width of the roadway opposite a standing motor vehicle shall be left for the free passage of other motor vehicles and a clear view of such stopped motor vehicle shall be available from a distance of 200 feet in each direction upon such roadway.
(b) This section shall not apply to the driver of any motor vehicle which is disabled while on the paved portion of a County road in such a manner and to such an extent that it is impossible to avoid stopping and temporarily leaving such disabled motor vehicle in such position.
(c) Whenever any Police Officer or Deputy Sheriff finds a vehicle in violation of this section, such Officer is authorized to move such motor vehicle, or require the driver or other person in charge of the motor vehicle to move the same to a position off the paved portion of the roadway. Any Police Officer or Deputy Sheriff is authorized to remove or cause to be removed to a place of safety any unattended motor vehicle illegally left standing upon the paved portion of any County road.
(d) Any person violating the terms of this section may be punished according to section 1-13. Jurisdiction over offenses under this section shall be in the Magistrate Court. Each day that a violation of this section shall continue shall be deemed a separate offense.
(Code 2005, § 58-1; Ord. of 2-9-1993, §§ 2—5)
1221:
Except as specifically authorized in section 32-22, it shall be unlawful:
(1) For any person to maintain 5 or more junk vehicles for more than 30 days (except vehicles being held pursuant to lawful impoundment by any law enforcement agency), without first obtaining and maintaining a valid State license, if applicable, a County permit, and complying with the requirements of this article.
(2) For any person to store, buy, sell and deal in junk vehicles, regardless of the number of junk vehicles involved, without first obtaining and maintaining a valid State license, if applicable, and a County permit, and complying with the requirements of this article.
(Code 2005, § 58-33; Ord. of 3-7-1989, art. IV, § 8)
1225:
The Walker County Community Connectivity Plan, which will be periodically updated, and its priorities, is adopted and shall serve to guide public and private policy to encourage greater access to broadband services throughout the County.
(Ord. No. O-01-25, 1-9-2025)
1228:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Applicant means a person applying for a permit for a broadband network project.
Application means a written request on the form(s) designated by the County for a permit for a broadband network project.
Broadband network project means any deployment of broadband services.
Permit means any local permit, license, certificate approval, registration, or similar form of approval required by policy, administrative rule, regulation, ordinance, or resolution with respect to a broadband network project.
(Ord. No. O-01-25, 1-9-2025)
1229:
The County shall appoint a single point of contact for all matters related to a broadband network project:
(1) The single point of contact shall be the Walker County Planning Director, who may be reached at 706-638-4048 or planning@walkerga.us.
(2) The single point of contact shall be available for matters related to a broadband network project or a related liaison who may direct such inquiry in real time, with general scope and responsibilities to include permitting and rights-of-way.
(3) The single point of contact information shall remain current with contact information updated within 15 calendar days of a change at walkercountyga.gov.
(Ord. No. O-01-25, 1-9-2025)
1230:
(a) The County shall determine whether an application is incomplete and notify the applicant, by email, of the determination by the County within 10 calendar days of receiving an application.
(b) If the County does not respond to the applicant on whether the application is incomplete, within 10 calendar days, the application shall be assumed to be complete on the 11th day.
(Ord. No. O-01-25, 1-9-2025)
1231:
(a) If the County determines that an application is not complete, the notification by email to the applicant shall specify all required components of the submitted application that were considered "incomplete"; and
(b) The County's response shall include a checklist of sequenced items that resulted in the application being deemed "incomplete" and the review timeline shall be as follows:
(1) The applicant has up to 40 calendar days from the date of notification of incompleteness to respond back with corrections; and
(2) If the applicant does not respond back within 40 calendar days, the application is deemed canceled.
(c) If within 10 calendar days the County does not respond to the applicant on whether the corrected application is incomplete, the application shall be assumed to be complete on the 11th day.
(d) The County shall require a new submission and reset the process and application fees, should an application be deemed incomplete a second time.
(Ord. No. O-01-25, 1-9-2025)
1233:
(a) Any fee imposed by the County to review an application, issue a permit, or perform any other activity related to a broadband network project shall be reasonable, cost based, and nondiscriminatory to all applicants.
(b) Any application fee that exceeds $100.00 shall be considered unreasonable, unless the County provides documentation justifying such fee based on a specific cost.
(Ord. No. O-01-25, 1-9-2025)
1234:
(a) Double fee. The County shall not require an application or permit(s) when already approved by an authorized state or federal jurisdiction. Provider shall notify and provide a copy of the approved permit to the single point-of-contact at the County prior to access of rights-of-way within the County's jurisdiction.
(b) Application validity timeline. Any approved application shall be valid for 6 months from the date of approval. Should a provider not commence the service request qualified in the approved application within 6 months, the application shall expire, and it shall require a new permit approval and any associated fees, as applicable.
(c) Single service drop. The County shall not require a permit for a broadband service provider to perform an installation of broadband service at an individual customer's service address as long as the facility being utilized only transverses a de minimis portion of the public right-of-way to reach the customer's property. The provider must still comply with the provisions of O.C.G.A. tit. 25, ch. 9.
(Ord. No. O-01-25, 1-9-2025)
1235:
Walker County acknowledges:
(1) A Georgia Certified Broadband Ready Community has an affirmative duty to notify the Georgia Department of Community Affairs of any changes to the information submitted as part of its application; and
(2) Failure to notify Georgia Department of Community Affairs of changes may result in revocation of Walker County's Broadband Ready Certification, should the certification be granted.
(Ord. No. O-01-25, 1-9-2025)
